rules.title: Nagaland: Inner Line Permit for everyone from outside
rules.detail: Anyone not indigenous to Nagaland needs one, applied for online. A domestic tourist permit costs 200 rupees for 30 days and is approved within four working hours.

source.title: Nagaland Inner Line Permit: frequently asked questions

history.change: All permit applications moved fully online, according to a state department page seen only as a search result.

source.title: Online Inner Line Permit (ILP)

rules.title: Nagaland: state permit also listed for foreign tourists
rules.detail: The official list of permit types includes a foreign tourist permit at 500 rupees for 30 days. This is separate from the central Protected Area Permit.

source.title: Nagaland Inner Line Permit: frequently asked questions

rules.title: Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram: Protected Area Permit for foreigners
rules.detail: Re-imposed in December 2024 after about 14 years of relaxation. Foreign citizens need prior permission and a Protected Area Permit before entering any of the three states.
rules.set_by: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India

rules.title: Dzukou Valley: entry run by a village youth body
rules.detail: The Southern Angami Youth Organisation admits visitors only through Viswema and Jakhama, collects an entry fee and requires identity cards. It is a community body, not a government office.

source.title: Dzukou valley now opens for visitors after weeks of closure

history.change: Valley reopened with rules: two entry points, identity card, authorised local guide for visitors from outside.

history.change: Trekking through both entry points suspended after a wildfire; reported 28 January 2026.

rules.title: Dimapur to Kohima: police diversions during landslides
rules.detail: When slides close the highway, Dimapur police send light vehicles over side roads, in 2025 between 6 am and 6 pm. The notices do not mention two-wheelers.

hazards.detail: Mudslides shut the highway at Chathe, Pagala Pahar and New Chumoukedima in September 2025, and at Pherima and Piphema in September 2024.

hazards.detail: A 2021 account says roads in northern Nagaland were bad enough that public transport to Mon ran through Assam by way of Sonari.

gaps: The date of 1 January 2025 for fully online permits comes from a search result; the state page returned a certificate error.
The official permit questions page does not say whether Dimapur is covered or where permits are checked.
How the state's foreign tourist permit fits with the Protected Area Permit re-imposed in December 2024 was not found on an official page.
No order of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the Protected Area Permit was opened; the rule rests on a news report and Mizoram's tourism site.
Reopening date of Dzukou Valley after the January 2026 fire seen only in a search snippet (19 February 2026) and not recorded.
A claim that a registered guide is compulsory for Dzukou since October 2025 appeared only in a search snippet.
Dzukou entry fee amounts come from news and an operator, not an official page, and are left out.
No source found on whether a motorcycle can be ridden from Viswema to the trailhead.
Highest point on the route and highway numbers beyond Kohima not sourced.
The Nagaland tourism site timed out and the Kohima district site shows no Dzukou or road notices.
Road condition north of Mokokchung rests on one 2021 blog; no recent source found.
